uncited: High-Frequency Aware Loss (LHF) is a perceptual regularization term designed to recover high-frequency details in rendered images while avoiding the texture distortion common in deeper perceptual losses.
It builds on [Perceptual Loss Training](2000-perceptual-loss-training.md) by specifically targeting the loss of high-frequency content that occurs when using pixel-wise losses on misaligned data.
This block consists of convolutional layers followed by ReLU activations but excludes any max-pooling layers.
*   Feature maps: The output of $F$ has dimensions $C \times W \times H$, where $C$ is the number of channels, and $W, H$ are the width and height of the feature map.
Extract features from the rendered patch $R$ using the shallow VGG block: $F_R = F(R)$.
Extract features from the aligned ground truth patch $G_i$: $F_{GT} = F(G_i)$.
Compute the squared Euclidean distance between the feature maps.
Normalize by the total number of elements in the feature map ($C \times W \times H$).
*   $\| \cdot \|_2^2$ denotes the squared L2 norm (sum of squared differences).
*   $C, W, H$ are the dimensions of the feature maps produced by $F$.
*   $G_i$ is the ground truth patch after alignment.
*   **Texture Distortion:** While deeper VGG losses distort textures, this shallow variant preserves them.
However, it is still sensitive to noise in rendered images, which can introduce optimization bias [S2].
*   **Time Complexity:** Depends on the forward pass of the first VGG-19 block.
Since it avoids pooling and deeper layers, it is computationally cheaper than full perceptual losses.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing feature maps from the first VGG block for both the rendered and ground truth patches.
*   **When not to use:** When computational resources are extremely limited and full VGG is too heavy (though this is lighter, it still requires a pre-trained model).
When the input images are very noisy, as it may introduce bias [S2].
The authors modified the original perceptual loss proposed by Johnson et al. [12] by using only the output of the first block of VGG-19 before max-pooling.
